Adames is the reigning WBC middleweight world champion but is tuning up for major title fights next year with a non-title bout against Warburton at a 165lb catchweight. Adames has an impressive track record. Undefeated at middleweight he's taken top-class wins over Sergiy Derevyanchenko, Julian Williams, Terrell Gausha and Austin Williams. He was unfortunate to be held to a draw against Hamzah Sheeraz, too. Warburton, a former Welsh champion, has not operated at that level, but this fight with Adames offers him a route to the elite end of the division, if he can score an upset. metadata.summary: England have hit back at Eddie Jones' claim they could be vulnerable to an upset by Japan on Saturday because they have one eye on their upcoming game with New Zealand.
metadata.content: England respond to Eddie Jones mind games ahead of Japan match in Nations Championship | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England respond to Eddie Jones mind games ahead of Japan match in Nations Championship England scrum coach Tom Harrison denied his side will be distracted by their upcoming game against New Zealand ahead of facing Eddie Jones' Japan on Saturday at Twickenham; Cadan Murley looking to play his "best rugby" and hold down place in starting line-up Friday 13 November 2026 17:10, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' James Cole previews the Nations Championship game between England and Japan as Eddie Jones returns to Twickenham. England have hit back at Eddie Jones' claim they could be vulnerable to an upset by Japan on Saturday because they have one eye on their upcoming game with New Zealand. Jones is aiming to disrupt Steve Borthwick's side by hitting them with the unexpected in the belief they will be "a little bit distracted" by the All Blacks' visit to Allianz Stadium on November 21. New Zealand are the box-office fixture of the campaign ahead of finals weekend but England deny they are looking beyond Japan. messages.text: Goalkeeper Owono given 12-match ban after De Miguel's death from collision

metadata.summary: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been suspended for 12 matches for his challenge of "excessive force" which resulted in the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.
metadata.content: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono given 12-match ban after Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel's death following collision | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Goalkeeper Jesus Owono given 12-match ban after Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel's death following collision Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel died after a collision with FC Andorra's goalkeeper Jesus Owono; the Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee has imposed the maximum punishment; the 2-2 scoreline will stand after the game was abandoned seven minutes into stoppage time Saturday 14 November 2026 08:13, UK Image: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono walks off the pitch after he collided with Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been suspended for 12 matches for his challenge of "excessive force" which resulted in the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel. The 25-year-old was sent off after colliding with De Miguel late in the Segunda Division game earlier this month. De Miguel died the following day . After a review of the incident the Spanish Football Federation's disciplinary committee imposed the maximum punishment on the Equatorial Guinea international. Viddal Riley will put himself on a path to a cruiserweight world title shot, if he can defend the European championship against Seydi Coupe on Saturday. Only 14 fights into his pro career, Riley is already rated as the IBF's No. 2 contender for their world championship. The Londoner wants to showcase himself as a world champion in waiting against Coupe. "I think I'm the most well-rounded cruiserweight in the world," Riley told Sky Sports . "I think we've trained for that because we want to cover every aspect of the game. We don't want to be lacking any area when it comes to movement, speed, IQ. All these things, I have them." Never out of the first two in 29 races, Nicky Henderson's charge is approaching veteran status at the age of 10 and was winning for the 21st time in his stellar career. His task was made easier with the late withdrawal of Gidleigh Park, but Mighty Bandit kept him honest after the last, with the 1-2 favourite pulling away again towards to line to win by two and a quarter lengths. Cobden said: "I'm so fortunate to be in this position riding all of these great horses and there's so many in the camp to look forward to, you do have to pinch yourself a little bit. "I was really looking forward to it and pressure is just something you put on yourself isn't it. There was no point having a sleepless night over a Shloer Chase though as what would I be like in March!" He went on: "I really enjoyed that. metadata.summary: Elina Svitolina defeated Aryna Sabalenka over three compelling sets to reach the semi-finals of the WTA Finals in Indian Wells.
metadata.content: WTA Finals: Elina Svitolina defeats Aryna Sabalenka to reach semi-finals as Mirra Andreeva overwhelms Diana Shnaider | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WTA Finals: Elina Svitolina defeats Aryna Sabalenka to reach semi-finals as Mirra Andreeva overwhelms Diana Shnaider Elina Svitolina has eliminated Aryna Sabalenka from the WTA Finals, winning in three sets, 6-3 ⁠3-6 ​6-1 after momentum swung from one to the other and back; Svitolina will face Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in the semi-finals at Indian Wells Tennis Garden Saturday 14 November 2026 07:30, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Aryna Sabalenka against Elina Svitolina in the WTA Finals. Elina Svitolina defeated Aryna Sabalenka over three compelling sets to reach the semi-finals of the WTA Finals in Indian Wells. The Ukrainian won 6-3 ⁠3-6 ​6-1, standing up to Sabalenka's powerful serve as she won the first set. Sabalenka stormed back to take control of the second set. But momentum shifted yet again in the deciding set. The opening games of the third were tight, but Svitolina landed a hammer blow when she broke Sabalenka's service game to go 3-1 up and pressed on from there to run away with the final set. "Very happy with the performance. It was not an easy match. It was a little bit of a roller coaster," Svitolina told Sky Sports .
